newsitem.title: ITALY: Tietmeyer says Germany has much to do before EMU.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says Germany has much to do before EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Friday Germany still had much to do to ensure it qualified for the planned European economic and monetary union (EMU).

In a pre-recorded interview with Italian television, Tietmeyer added that Germany wanted Italy to join in the first wave of countries signing up to the single European currency, but it would have to respect the Maastricht criteria.

Asked if Germany would make the grade for EMU when the founder members were selected next year, Tietmeyer said: "I hope so very much, but we still have a great deal to do. We find ourselves in a difficult situation at the moment.

"There are a series of parameters which we are not meeting," he said, speaking through an interpreter from his Frankfurt office. He added that German membership would depend on "sufficient" progress being made to meet the targets.

Asked if Germans did not want Italy to join EMU, Tietmeyer replied: "Your assumption is false...we really do want Italy to take part, naturally on the basis of what the treaty envisages...obviously there'll be no privileges and no discrimination. That is not possible either for Italy or Germany."

The Bundesbank President added that both Italy and Germany had to meet the criteria laid down by the Maastricht Treaty on a "lasting basis". Founder EMU members are due to be choosen in May 1998 with the single currency scheduled for launch in 1999.
